DILG • Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle. Quezon City http: Ilwww. dilg gov.ph DILG Legal Opinion No. IO, series of 2016 12 FEB HON. MONICO O. PUENTEVELLA Elected Mayor Bacolod City, Negros Occidental Dear Hon. Puentevella: 'This has reference to your letter requesting the Department's definitive legal opinion on the following issues: 2. 3. Is the filling up of vacancies allowed in a re-enacted budget? Is an Acting Mayor, especially in the last few days of his term, authorized to fill up vacancies during the period of' a re- enacted budget? Is the filling up of vacancies allowed during the period ofa re- enacted budget under a Mayor who is exercising his/her position in an acting capacity?" We shall answer your queries in one (1) discussion since they are interrelated. At the outset, may we invite your attention to Section 46 (a) of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991, thus: "Section 46. Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension Trom office, the vice-governor, city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint. suspend, or dismiss which can onl be exercised if the riodoftem Inca ci em Io exceeds thirty (30) working days. "(Emphasis Supplied) Based on the foregoing, the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees can be exercised by the acting Mayor only if the period of temporary incapacity of the elected Mayor exceeds thirty (30) working days.

If it is apparent that the incapacity, as in the case of herein legal incapacity due to suspension from office, will exceed thirty (30) working days, then it follows that the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees may already be exercised even prior to the expiration of the thirty-day period. However, the foregoing rule should be read in relation to the Section 323 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR): 'SECTION 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the Sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of' the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its membezs, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. IT the sanggunian stifl Tails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations OT the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. However, only the annual ro Hati ns for alaries an es of existin itions statuto and contractual obli tions and e entia/ o in ex ns auth rized in the annual and su lementalb etS for the edin year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. In the implementation of' such reenacted ordinance, the local treasurer concerned Shal/ exclude Trom the estimates of income for the preceding fiscal year those realized from nonrecurring sources, like na [iona/ aids, proceeds from loans, sale of assets, prior year adjustments, and other analogous sources of income. No ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations Shal/ be passed in place of' the annual appropriations. In case the revised income estimates be less [han the aggregate reenacted appropriations, the local treasurer concerned shall accordingly advise the sanggunian concerned which shall, within ten (IO) days from the receipt of' such advice, make the necessary adjustments or reductions. The revisedappropriationsauthorized by the sanggunian concerned shall then be the basis Tor disbursements. (Emphasis Supplied)

"ART. 415. Budget Authorization. xxx In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted. xxx Only the annual appropriations Tor salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shah' be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds Shai/ be in accordance therewith. The aforequoted provisions clearly provide the consequence in case the Sanggunian fails to enact the annual appropriations, that is, the budget of the preceding year is reenacted. In case of reenacted budget, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted. This was reiterated by the Supreme Court in the case of Villanueva vs. Oplel. A reenacted budget will have implied disadvantages, as enumerated in the DBM's Budget Operations Manual (BOM) for Local Government Units (An Updated Version of the June 2005 Edition), such as but not limited to, the following: 1) No creation of positions; 2) New programs, projects and activities; 3) No utilization of the increase in IRA allocation for the year since the same is not covered by an Appropriation Ordinance; 4) Non-implementation of non-recurring activities no matter how vital they may be; 5) No supplemental appropriations. While it is true that in DILG Legal Opinion Nos. 30, series of 2011 and 22, series of 2012 the Department mentioned "no filling of positions, "as one of the disadvantages in a reenacted budget, we refer only to the filling up of "newly created positions, "therefore excluding those positions that were long before created only that, through the years, they are not filled up. Please note that in the aforesaid DILG Legal Opinions, the phrase "no filling of positions, "always follows the phrase "no creation of positions". Along this line, in Legal Opinion No. L-B-2001-13, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) had the opportunity to clarify what is included in the phrase "salaries and wages ofexisting positions 't thus 1 G.R. No. 165125, 18 November 2005.

"In sum, only the annual appropriations Tor salaries and wages of existing positions authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets Tor the preceding year are deemed reenacted. Stated otherwise. the salaries and wages of existing positions refer to those actually charged against Persona/ Services account such as. 'salaries of permanent positions 'and lump sum for 'contractual. casual and emergency-personnel! (Emphasis Supplied) Notably, salaries of vacant positions in the government are still being funded in the annual appropriations of a local government unit and thus may be properly considered " existing positions ". Given the above disquisition and in reply to your queries, the Acting Mayor may fill up vacancies in the City Government of Bacolod, notwithstanding a reenacted budget, provided however that the positions to be filled up are not newly created positions. We hope to have guided you accordingly. 18/17 Copy furnished: DIR. MARGIE A. BILIGAN Officer-in-Charge, DILG-Negros Island Region Negros Occidental Provincial Office PAC Bldg.
